question: What are the products in a reaction where an acid reacts with a base?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A reaction in which an **acid** reacts with a **base** is termed a **Neutralization reaction**.
 
• In this process, the **hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid and the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** from the base combine to form **water (H2O)**.
 
• The remaining part of the acid (anion) and the base (cation) combine to produce an **ionic compound** known as a **salt**.
 
• The general chemical equation for this reaction is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**. ***Hence, the correct option is Salt and water.***
 
• Neutralization reactions are typically **exothermic**, meaning **heat** is evolved during the reaction, which often raises the temperature of the reaction mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of Neutralization:**

 
 
• The reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** produces **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** and **water**. The formula is: **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O**.
 
• Another common example is the reaction between **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** to form **Potassium sulfate (K2SO4)** and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Salts:**
 
 
• If a **strong acid** reacts with a **strong base**, the resulting salt is **neutral** (pH value of **7**).
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **weak base** produces an **acidic salt** (pH value **less than 7**).
 
• A **weak acid** reacting with a **strong base** results in a **basic salt** (pH value **greater than 7**).
 
 
 
• **Real-world Applications:**
 
 
• **Indigestion:** Our stomach produces **hydrochloric acid** to digest food. Excess acid causes **acidity**, which is neutralized by taking **antacids** like **Milk of Magnesia** (Magnesium hydroxide), which is a **base**.
 
• **Ant Stings:** The sting of an ant contains **formic acid**. The effect of the sting can be neutralized by rubbing moist **baking soda** (sodium hydrogen carbonate) or **calamine solution** (zinc carbonate), which are **basic** in nature.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** Plants do not grow well if the **soil** is too acidic or too basic. Acidic soil is treated with **bases** like **quicklime** (calcium oxide) or **slaked lime** (calcium hydroxide).
 
• **Factory Waste:** Many **factories** discharge acidic wastes. These are neutralized by adding **basic substances** before being disposed of into water bodies to protect **aquatic life**.
